readAfter: adjudication.json was written, and score-skill-go.json, score-skill.json and the analyses were computed. The reader is the corpus author, who also designed the arm and had seen the scores. Reading can add observations; it changes no as-run number.
procedure: As v3-run-skill-go/PREREGISTRATION.md fixes it: (1) every evidence-gap twin skill-go judged GO, (2) every defect twin without NO_GO, (3) every sound plan with NO_GO, (4) a sample of up to ten sound plans skill-go still judged CHANGES_RECOMMENDED, (5) a sample of up to ten evidence-gap twins skill-go judged NO_GO, (6) a sample of up to ten it judged correctly. Reports were read in the saved text (truncated at 1,100 to 2,200 characters for the long ones, with the machine summary where it fits); the packets were read for (4).

5_overclaimedGapTwins.rule: one per family with any (rate_limit_quota, rollback_window, upgrade_compat, retry_idempotent, payload_limit), then second observations in the order rate_limit_quota, rollback_window, upgrade_compat, retry_idempotent, payload_limit

6_correctGapTwins.rule: one per family with any (storage_access, unique_constraint, retry_idempotent, upgrade_compat, payload_limit, capacity_headroom, rollback_window), then second observations of capacity_headroom, storage_access and unique_constraint

findings.none_waved_through: No evidence-gap twin was judged GO, no defect twin lacked NO_GO and no sound plan was judged NO_GO, so readings 1 to 3 have nothing to read. The v2 mechanism of the sentence arm (a named gap recast as optional, one of 32 observations in defined-go) did not occur once in 32 skill-go observations.
findings.theRemainingHedge: skill-go trial 1, unique_constraint B (Q-497363): CHANGES_RECOMMENDED with one UNVERIFIED RISK on line 5 (the 'single code path' claim has no query behind it for rows since 4.9, and imports, admin tools or direct SQL could bypass it) and a CANNOT_CHECK NOTE on the concurrent index build. It is the same residual gap the skill-style arm and the Gemini reviewer raised on this plan family, a defensible reading, and no blocker. It is the only hedge among 64 sound-plan observations (skill-style control: 29).
findings.overclaimedGapTwins: All ten reports name the unestablished fact correctly and quote the line that states it, and in nine the report says in so many words that it is not claiming the failure will happen ('I am not claiming the callers will break', 'no overrun is asserted here', 'This is not a guess about the data') and then rules it a BLOCKER | VERIFIED because the plan admits it has no evidence and the stakes are hard or irreversible ('the blocker is narrower', 'a release should not proceed under those conditions', 'a blocker rather than a robustness suggestion'). The VERIFIED label sits on the line that states the gap, which is why the scorer's unsupported-VERIFIED gate is zero: the quotation is on the cited line. In the corpus's terms, and under the review contract's rule that missing evidence is not a proven defect, this is an overclaim; a reader could argue that an admitted-unverified requirement with a contractual penalty or an irreversible effect deserves a blocker, and the Gemini reviewer and the correct skill-go reports (below) did not. Each overclaim asks for the same check the correct reports ask for. Seven twins were overclaimed in each trial, five of them the same cases (nine distinct cases in all; 59 of 64 verdicts identical across trials), so it is largely a per-case disposition, not noise.
findings.correctGapTwins: All ten name the gap, tie it to the plan's stated requirement and the cost of being wrong, say it is a risk and not a proven defect, and ask for a measurement or a confirmation. Eight of the ten add a sentence that echoes the added line, for example 'a needed change, not just extra robustness', 'a change the plan needs, not an optional improvement', 'more than an optional robustness tweak'. The sentence makes the reviewer decide explicitly whether a gap is optional or needed; for a stated unknown that decides the plan's success it concludes 'needed', and the report then either stays at a risk (the correct verdict) or goes on to a blocker (the overclaim).
findings.interpretation: A reading, not a measured mechanism: the added sentence draws a line between 'optional suggestion' (NO_BLOCKERS_FOUND) and 'needed change', and gives the reviewer no place for a needed change that is still not a blocker. The skill-style prompt had no such line and hedged everything; with the line, hedges disappear for sound plans (their suggestions are optional) and a share of the gap twins moves up to BLOCKERS_FOUND (their gap is needed). The CHANGES_RECOMMENDED verdict survives for the twins whose report keeps 'needed' at the level of a RISK (18 of 32).

limits: A reading by the corpus author who designed the arm, after the scores. Ten of 14 overclaimed and ten of 18 correct gap twins and the one hedged sound plan were read; the other reports only through their verdicts, findings and the keyword rubric (recall only: the gap named in 27 of 32 skill-go twins, 30 of 32 in the control, 27 of 32 in the earlier skill-style run; every report read named it). Corpus v3 had been seen for this question and, in every evidence-gap family, the plan states the unknown in one explicit sentence.
